note: All reaction chemistry lives here. Edit this file to add/remove/fix reactions. No reaction-specific code in the engine.

templates.name: Kinetic enolate formation
templates.provenance: Ported from original MolecularReactivityEngine.execute_first_principles_step pathway A. Chemistry: Fleming, I. 'Molecular Orbitals and Organic Chemical Reactions' (2010). Strong hindered bases (LDA, t-BuOK) deprotonate the alpha-carbon to give the enolate; branching over all alpha positions shows both kinetic and thermodynamic isomers.

templates.name: E2 beta-elimination (HBr)
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. 'A Collection of Robust Organic Synthesis Reactions for In Silico Molecule Design' J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Anti-periplanar E2 elimination: strong base abstracts beta-H while bromide departs.

templates.name: E2 beta-elimination (HCl)
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Anti-periplanar E2 elimination with chloride leaving group.

templates.name: E2 beta-elimination (HI)
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. E2 elimination with iodide leaving group; highly favored due to weak C-I bond.

templates.name: SN2: alkyl bromide + hydroxide
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Classic SN2 nucleophilic substitution: hydroxide displaces bromide at sp3 carbon with inversion of configuration. Nucleophile left unmapped in product to avoid charge inheritance issues.

templates.name: SN2: alkyl chloride + hydroxide
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. SN2 with hydroxide on chloride substrate.

templates.name: Hydrolysis: alkyl bromide + water
templates.provenance: Adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Net product of SN1/SN2 hydrolysis. Proton transfer from oxonium intermediate is implicit; net product is the alcohol.

templates.name: Hydrolysis: alkyl chloride + water
templates.provenance: Adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Net product of SN1/SN2 hydrolysis with chloride leaving group.

templates.name: Finkelstein reaction (Br -> I)
templates.provenance: Finkelstein, H. Ber. Dtsch. Chem. Ges. 1910, 43, 1528. Halide metathesis driven by NaI precipitation. SMARTS adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098.

templates.name: Finkelstein reaction (Cl -> I)
templates.provenance: Finkelstein, H. Ber. Dtsch. Chem. Ges. 1910, 43, 1528. Halide exchange from chloride. SMARTS from Hartenfeller M. et al. 2011.

templates.name: Williamson ether synthesis (bromide + alkoxide)
templates.provenance: Williamson, A.W. J. Chem. Soc. 1852, 4, 229. SN2 of alkoxide on alkyl bromide to form ether. O left unmapped in product to avoid charge inheritance; electrophilic C (:1) and alkoxide C (:3) are both mapped.

templates.name: Williamson ether synthesis (chloride + alkoxide)
templates.provenance: Williamson, A.W. J. Chem. Soc. 1852, 4, 229. SN2 of alkoxide on alkyl chloride. SMARTS adapted from Hartenfeller M. et al. 2011.

templates.name: Enolate protonation (protic workup)
templates.provenance: Standard enolate quench with protic solvent. Chemistry: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. 1-reactant template (protic condition gates when it fires on enolate intermediates); :2 unmapped in product to add fresh neutral carbonyl O.

templates.name: Halide exchange (Br -> Cl)
templates.provenance: Adapted from Finkelstein-type halide metathesis. Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. Thermodynamically less favorable than Br->I (Keq < 1 in most solvents) but possible under forcing conditions with NaCl.

templates.name: N-alkylation: alkyl bromide + ammonia
templates.provenance: Hartenfeller M. et al. J. Chem. Inf. Model. 2011, 51, 3093-3098. N-alkylation producing ammonium salt; proton transfer gives amine.

templates.name: Carbonyl gem-diol formation (hydration)
templates.provenance: March, J. 'Advanced Organic Chemistry' 5th ed. Reversible nucleophilic addition of water to carbonyl to give gem-diol. Equilibrium strongly disfavored for ketones (Keq << 1) but thermodynamically accessible for aldehydes.
